academic_translation:
In that way, you have handed me over time and again,
And I have suffered for a long time;
I, remembering those grudges,
Will destroy your thinking of your own welfare.
translation: You have handed me over to suffering again and again. I have hurt for a long time. I remember those grudges. Now I will destroy your thoughts about your own good.

academic_translation:
If I wish to be happy,
I should not take delight in myself.
If I wish to protect myself,
I should always protect others.
translation: If I wish to be happy, I should not delight in myself. If I wish to protect myself, I should always protect others.

academic_translation:
To whatever extent this body
Is completely cared for,
To that same extent it falls
Into becoming extremely fragile.
translation: The more this body is completely cared for, the more fragile it becomes.

academic_translation:
Even when it has fallen in that way,
If its desires cannot be fulfilled
By this entire earth,
Who can fulfill its desires?
translation: Once it becomes weak like that, even the whole earth cannot fulfill its desires. Who else could give it what it wants?

academic_translation:
From desiring the impossible, afflictions
and a deteriorated intention will also arise.
Whoever does not depend on anything,
their excellence is inexhaustible.
translation: Wanting impossible things brings troubling emotions and ruins good intentions. But when someone does not depend on anything, their excellence will never run out.

academic_translation:
Therefore, one should not give an opportunity
For the desires of the body to increase.
Whatever attractive thing one does not grasp,
That is an excellent thing.
translation: Therefore, I should not let the desires of the body grow. Not grabbing onto attractive things is an excellent thing.

academic_translation:
Ultimately reaching its end in ashes,
Motionless, it is moved by another;
An impure and unbearable form—
Why do I direct grasping at self toward this?
translation: In the end, it will just turn to ashes. It cannot move unless something else moves it. This form is dirty and hard to bear. Why do I keep grabbing hold of a self in this?

academic_translation:
Whether it is alive or whether it is dead,
What use to me is this machine?
If it is no different from a clod of earth and the like,
Alas, why do I not dispel my pride?
translation: Whether it is alive or dead, what use is this machine to me? If it is no different from a lump of dirt, oh, why do I not get rid of my pride?

academic_translation:
By tending to the body,
Having accumulated meaningless suffering,
Attachment and anger—
What use are they toward this, which is similar to wood?
translation: By taking care of the body, I have only built up useless suffering. What is the point of clinging and anger toward this thing that is just like wood?

academic_translation:
Whether it is nurtured by me in this way,
Or eaten by vultures and the like,
Since it has no attachment and no hatred,
Why do I have attachment toward it?
translation: It does not matter if I take good care of it, or if vultures eat it. Since it has no clinging and no hatred, why do I feel clinging toward it?

academic_translation:
That which is angered by blame,
And that which is delighted by praise—
If it itself knows nothing,
For whose sake have I toiled?
translation: If the thing that gets angry at blame and happy at praise actually knows nothing at all, then who have I worked so hard for?

academic_translation:
Whoever desires this body,
If I say, "They and I are friends,"
Since everyone desires their own body,
Why do I not delight in them?
translation: If I say that anyone who desires this body is my friend, then why do I not delight in everyone? After all, everyone desires their own body.

academic_translation:
Therefore, without attachment, I
Shall give up the body to benefit beings.
Thus, although it has many faults,
I shall retain it like an instrument for action.
translation: So, without being attached, I will give up my body to help others. It has many faults. Still, I will keep it like a tool for doing good.

academic_translation:
Therefore, enough of childish behavior!
I shall follow in the footsteps of the wise,
And having recalled the discourse on heedfulness,
I shall dispel sleep and mental dullness.
translation: I have had enough of acting like a child! I will follow the wise. I will remember the teachings on carefulness. I will chase away sleep and dullness of mind.

academic_translation:
Therefore, in order to clear away obscurations,
Having withdrawn my mind from mistaken paths,
Constantly upon the perfect object of focus,
I shall rest in meditative equipoise.
translation: To clear away the veil, I will turn my mind away from wrong paths. I will always rest by settling the mind on the perfect thing to focus on.

academic_translation: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the eighth chapter, called Meditative Concentration.

locked_terms.use: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero

translation: From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, the eighth chapter, called Calm Focus.

academic_translation:
All these branches
The Sage taught for the sake of wisdom.
Therefore, those who wish to pacify suffering
Should generate wisdom.
translation: The Sage taught all these branches for the sake of wisdom. So, anyone who wants to stop suffering should grow wisdom.

academic_translation:
Conventional truth and ultimate truth:
These are held to be the two truths.
Ultimate truth is not the domain of the intellect;
The intellect is said to be conventional truth.
translation: People believe in two truths. They are everyday truth and deepest truth. Deepest truth is beyond the reach of the thinking mind. The thinking mind is just everyday truth.

academic_translation:
In this regard, two kinds of world are seen:
Yogis and ordinary people.
In this regard, the ordinary world
Is invalidated by the world of yogis;
translation: We see two kinds of worlds. There is the world of the meditation master and the world of ordinary people. The world of the meditation master proves the ordinary world wrong.

academic_translation:
Even yogis, due to differences in intellect,
are invalidated by those successively higher,
through examples accepted by both,
because, for the sake of the result, they are not analyzed.
translation: Even a meditation master has a different level of thinking mind. Higher masters prove the lower ones wrong. They use examples they both agree on. They do not question these examples because they just want a result.

academic_translation:
Worldly persons see entities,
And conceptualize them as true reality,
Not as being like illusions; therefore, here,
Yogis and the world dispute.
translation: A person of the world sees a thing and believes it is what is truly real. They do not see that it is like an illusion. Because of this, the meditation master argues with the world.

academic_translation:
Even the direct perception of forms and so forth
Is through convention, not through valid cognition.
That is false, just as the convention of purity and so forth
Regarding impurity and so forth is false.
translation: Seeing directly a shape and other things is just common usage. It is not a reliable way of knowing. It is false, just like the common usage that calls filth by the name of cleanness.

academic_translation:
For the sake of guiding the world,
The Protector taught entities; in reality,
They are not momentary.
If one objects, "This contradicts even conventional truth,"
translation: To guide the world, the Protector taught about a thing. But in reality, things are not lasting only a moment. Someone might say, "This goes against even everyday truth!"

academic_translation:
There is no fault in the conventional truth of yogis;
In relation to the world, they see reality.
Otherwise, regarding women as impure,
That realization would be invalidated by the world.
translation: There is no mistake in the everyday truth of a meditator. Compared to the world, they see the way things really are. Otherwise, when they see women as unclean, the world would prove them wrong.

academic_translation:
"How is there merit from a Victor like an illusion?"
Just as it is for one who is truly existent.
"If sentient beings are like illusions,
How are they born after dying?"
translation: Someone might ask, "How do we get a store of goodness from a Victorious One who is like an illusion?" It is just like getting it from someone who is really existing. They might also ask, "If living beings are like illusions, how are they born again after they die?"

academic_translation:
As long as conditions are assembled,
For that long even an illusion will arise.
Merely because of a long continuum, how
Can a sentient being be truly existent?
translation: As long as the circumstances come together, an illusion will appear for that long. Just because they have a long unbroken flow, how can a living being be truly existing?

academic_translation:
In killing an illusory person and the like,
Because there is no mind, there is no misdeed;
But toward one possessing an illusory mind,
Merit and misdeed arise.
translation: Killing a person made by magic is not a harmful deed, because they have no mind. But when acting toward someone who has the mind of an illusion, a store of goodness and a harmful deed can happen.

academic_translation:
Because mantras and so forth lack the capacity,
An illusory mind does not arise.
Arising from various conditions,
That illusion itself is of various kinds.
translation: Because things like sacred words do not have the power, the mind of an illusion does not appear. Because it comes from many different circumstances, that illusion itself comes in many different kinds.

academic_translation:
Nowhere is there a single condition
That is capable of everything.
"If ultimate truth is nirvāṇa,
And saṃsāra is conventional truth, then
translation: There is no single circumstance anywhere that has the power to do everything. Someone might say, "If the deepest truth is freedom from sorrow, and the cycle of rebirth is everyday truth, then..."

academic_translation:
"Since even a Buddha would cycle [in saṃsāra],
What is the use of the conduct of awakening?"
If the continuum of conditions is not severed,
Even an illusion does not cease;
translation: Someone might say, "Since even a Buddha would be trapped in the world, what is the use of the way of acting for awakening?" I reply: As long as the unbroken flow of circumstances is not cut, even an illusion will not stop.

academic_translation:
But because the continuum of conditions is severed,
It does not arise even in conventional truth.
"When even error does not exist,
By what will an illusion be perceived?"
translation: But when the unbroken flow of circumstances is cut, it does not happen even in everyday truth. Someone might ask, "When even the mistake does not exist, what will see the illusion?"

academic_translation:
When for you the illusion itself
Does not exist, then what is perceived?
"If in reality another exists,
That aspect is the mind itself."

locked_terms.use: in the way things really are

translation: I reply, "When you say the illusion itself does not exist, then what is seen?" Someone might answer, "If something else exists in the way things really are, that way it appears is the mind itself."

academic_translation:
When the mind itself is an illusion,
Then what is seen by what?
Even the Protector of the world
Stated that the mind does not see the mind.
translation: If the mind itself is an illusion, then what is seen by what? Even the Protector of the world taught that the mind cannot see the mind.

academic_translation:
Just as the blade of a sword
Does not cut itself, so too the mind.
"If [you say], just as a lamp
Perfectly illuminates its own entity,"
translation: Just as a sword blade cannot cut itself, the mind cannot see itself. Someone might say, "But a lamp lights itself up perfectly!"

academic_translation:
A lamp is not something to be illuminated,
Because it is not obscured by darkness.
"Unlike a crystal, a blue thing
Does not depend on another for its blueness."
translation: A lamp does not need to be lit up, because darkness does not hide it. Someone might argue, "Unlike a clear crystal, a blue thing does not depend on anything else for its blueness."

academic_translation:
"Likewise, some things are seen to depend
On others, and some to not depend."
When it is not blue itself,
That is not made blue by itself.
translation: Someone might say, "We see that some things depend on other things, and some do not." But something that is not blue cannot make itself blue.

academic_translation:
If it is known by consciousness and thus expressed,
"The lamp makes things luminous,"
Having been known by what is it thus expressed,
"The intellect itself is luminous"?
translation: When awareness knows a lamp, we can say, "The lamp is shining." But what knows the thinking mind so we can say, "The thinking mind itself is shining"?

academic_translation:
When it is not seen by anyone at all,
Whether it is luminous or not luminous,
Like the alluring pose of a barren woman's daughter,
Even to express it is meaningless.

locked_terms.use: daughter of a woman with no children

translation: If no one sees it at all, it means nothing to say whether it is shining or not. It is like talking about the beautiful pose of the daughter of a woman with no children.

academic_translation:
"If self-awareness does not exist,
How does the memory of consciousness occur?"
From its connection to experiencing another,
Memory arises, like the poison of a rat.
translation: Someone might ask, "If there is no awareness of itself, how can we have a memory of awareness?" A memory happens because it is connected to experiencing something else. It is like the poison of a rat.

academic_translation:
"If, because one endowed with other conditions sees,
it is luminous to itself,"
through the application of accomplished eye ointment,
the vase is seen, but not the eye ointment itself.
translation: Someone might say, "Because of a special circumstance, a person can see that the mind shines to itself." But using magic eye ointment lets you see a hidden vase. It does not let you see the eye ointment itself.
